content: {"summary":"On 15 Oct 2025 the catalog‑api connection pool filled because a long‑running weekly export transaction held a lock on the products table, causing subsequent queries (and a pending ALTER) to wait and exhaust the pool.","likely_cause":"Long‑running weekly export transaction holding an ACCESS SHARE lock on products, leading to lock contention and connection‑pool exhaustion.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The weekly export transaction held an ACCESS SHARE lock on products, preventing other statements from acquiring connections.","evidence_ids":["RB-028#2"],"quote":"The weekly export begins. Its open transaction holds an `ACCESS SHARE` lock on `products` until it ends."},{"text":"30 catalog_app sessions were blocked by the ALTER's pid, filling the pool to its limit.","evidence_ids":["RB-028#4"],"quote":"Then 30 `catalog_app` sessions, each blocked by the ALTER's pid."},{"text":"Slow work on catalog-db kept connections checked out far beyond their usual short stay, contributing to pool exhaustion.","evidence_ids":["INC-0091#1"],"quote":"What kept the connections busy was slow work on catalog-db."}],"next_checks":["Query pg_stat_activity to confirm the export transaction duration during the incident window","Check for any other long‑running queries or lock contention in the same period","Verify that the migration was cancelled and not retried inadvertently","Implement monitoring alerts for sudden spikes in pool usage"]}
